doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Armstrong, the boats and the downtown halls
title: The McCullen and Humphrey family bands, c. 1908
summary: Martin recalls the McCullens and the Humphrey brothers, who had a tough band around 1908. Tom played with them and took one lesson from the old man, Jim Humphrey.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah. And now you take, back, 1908. Back, all back up in there. You take McCullen and, they had a tough band. McCullen and, Old Man McCullen. McCullen and Poissy's daddy. Brother Humphrey? Yeah, he's together. Willie Humphrey. Yeah, he's together. See?
Oh, I played with them too. I had him played with me too. The old man, the young man, the two brothers. I played with them all.
Their grandfather was Jim Humphrey, wasn't he? He was a teacher, I think. Yeah, that's the old man.
I went to the old fella, old fella, and took one lesson with him with the clan that. And I went back no more.
Well, that's a long time though.
